description:
(Summary from jobright.ai; the original posting may say more.)

Stanford University’s Solomon and Keller laboratories in Psychiatry and Behavioral Sciences seek a Software Developer Associate to build and maintain software for managing, accessing, and analyzing human electrophysiological data. The role also contributes to software for brain stimulation research, supports TMS experiments, and develops documentation and user resources.
Software Developer Associate assisting Python package/API development for electrophysiology analysis and TMS experiment software integration and refinement

Responsibilities:
• Assessment of users needs relating to the flexible access and analysis of human electrophysiology data and associated research metadata
• Assist in the development of new Python-based software packages and APIs to enable easy, efficient, and fast analysis of these data
• Assist in the integration of new software with in-house and Stanford-based data storage solutions
• Contribute to refinements of existing software packages for conducting transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) research experiments, including hardware/software interfacing and GUI development
• Real-time technical support and troubleshooting during TMS experiments
• Develop user guides and tutorials for newly-developed software and follow best practices for code documentation and version control
• Follow team software development methodology
• Suggest improvements and/or changes to help increase efficiency
• Assess user needs and requirements
• Assist with design and development of applications that may
  involve sophisticated data manipulation
• Assist with maintaining and updating existing programs
• Troubleshoot and solve basic technical problems
• Assist in the design and implementation of user and operations
  training programs
• Contribute to documenting changes in software for end
  users
• Follow team software development methodology
• Suggest improvements and/or changes to help increase
  efficiency

Requirements:
• Bachelor's degree or a combination of education and relevant
experience
• Familiarity with latest software and design standards
• Ability to solve logical problems for technical
applications
• Knowledge of and ability to select, adapt, and effectively use
programming methods
• Ability to recognize and recommend needed changes in user and/or
operations procedures
• Basic knowledge of software engineering principles
• Strong knowledge of at least one programming language

Preferred:
• Prior experience working with or developing software to process biological time-series data
• Experience with Python and MATLAB programming languages
• Experience with Github
• General knowledge of privacy standards for handling health-related information
